name: Supply/Demand Zone Strategy [Manual Build]
raw_text: Supply/Demand Zone Strategy -- manually constructed by Claude Code, reading the source document directly. No strategy_parser.py, no ai_integration/ used to build these conditions. Built using 3 NEW engine capabilities added specifically for this strategy (see concepts.consolidation_impulse_zones, concepts.valid_structure_trend, and the demand_zone/supply_zone re-entry containment check in configured_strategy.py), each covered by real unit tests in tests/test_supply_demand_zone_capabilities.py using synthetic OHLC data. Trend structure (Step 1 + Rule 2 + Rule 3: uptrend persists until the specific 'valid low' -- validated by a prior break of structure -- is itself broken, not on every minor lower low) is represented exactly via valid_structure_trend(), a genuine sequential state machine, not an approximation. Demand/supply zones (a multi-bar consolidation immediately before a sharp impulsive move) are represented exactly via consolidation_impulse_zones() -- tightness measured as the window's own range vs. the average single-bar range (<=1.5x), impulse measured as the next bar's move vs. ATR(14) (>=1.5x ATR) while actually clearing the consolidation's boundary. Zone re-entry (Rule 8/9) is a real fresh-every-bar containment check, not an existence check. Stop-loss (Rule 10/11, 'right below the demand zone'/'above the supply zone') reads the SAME zone the entry re-entered, via a small, targeted extension to the existing structure-type SL candidate chain (entry_demand_low/entry_supply_high checked first, generic order-block/support-resistance fallbacks unchanged for every other strategy). Take-profit (Rule 12/13, 'recent highs/lows') uses the existing structure-type TP chain's final fallback (entry_resistance/entry_support, built from confirmed swing points) since no order_block/fvg concepts are declared here -- flagged as an approximation of 'recent highs', a swing-based reading rather than a literal N-bar rolling high/low. The pre-trade R:R>2.5 filter (Rule 14/15) uses the existing min_risk_reward_filter + primary_target_lookback_bars mechanism (20-bar highest-high/lowest-low lookback as the 'recent highs/lows' reference for the FILTER specifically) -- note this is a SEPARATE reference point from the actual take-profit target above; both independently approximate 'recent highs' using the two different existing primitives available for a pre-trade filter vs. an actual exit target, not a contradiction, but not numerically identical either. Trend filter (Rule 16, never sell in an uptrend / never buy in a downtrend) is satisfied by construction: long requires a bullish valid_structure_trend reading, short requires bearish -- never both. Timeframe (Rule 18, not specified in source): 1-hour used for both analysis and entry, my own scope decision. Risk % per trade (Rule 20, not specified): 1% used, my own default. Session/timing rules (Rule 19, not specified): not represented. No indicators used at all (Rule 17), matching the source's explicit 'pure price action, no indicators' -- indicators=[] is empty.
